text:
Sara: Quick proposal — treat KV cache hits for the reranker as "opportunistic" routing candidates. Idea: if a prefix KV hit avoids most model work we can route to cheaper nodes and reflect that in effective per-request pricing. Thoughts?
Dan: what exactly do you mean by "opportunistic" here? free-routing vs policy-controlled?
Priya: my read: we prefer cache-first routing, but only when hit coverage > X% so quality unaffected. Pricing: cache-hit portion shouldn't bill full model token cost.
Josh: main edge: partial hits where we still need to run the model for tail tokens. How do we attribute cost? split billing?
Lee: telemetry requirement: show hit-rate, coverage (percent tokens saved), per-tenant and per-route. Console needs to expose hit breakdown. Otherwise ops can't reason about cost changes.
Sara: exactly. UX idea: console shows "effective token cost" = model_token_cost * (1 - hit_coverage) + hit_unit. Give knob: prefer "latency" (route to hot low-latency cache nodes) or "cost" (route to cold cheaper nodes if cached).
Dan: billing policy proposals: (A) treat hits as zero-cost (B) charge small fixed unit per hit (C) prorate by tokens avoided. I'm leaning B for simplicity.
Priya: I'd avoid zero-cost; it breaks economics and can be gamed. B or C both workable. C is accurate but complexity for billing infra.
Josh: from routing side we can implement policy chain: 1) exact KV route -> 2) low-cost quantized model if partial -> 3) primary model fallback. We need to encode that order into route policy. Example proto:```json
{"policy": [{"type": "kv_cache_preference", "min_coverage": 0.7}, {"type": "model_variant", "tier": "cheap-quant"}, {"type": "model_variant", "tier": "full"}]}
```
Lee: security/ops note: opportunistic cache routing increases surface for cache-exhaustion attacks. Add per-tenant TTLs and auth checks, and rate-limit cache lookups to avoid amplification.
Sara: quotas question — should cache hits consume quota units? If we count them against heavy-model quota, tenants could exhaust cheap-route benefits. Proposal: charge small "cache units" that don't decrement model quota but do decrement a separate cheap-cache quota.
Dan: console UX: show two quota bars: "Model compute quota" and "Cache quota" with rollover settings. Also show estimated monthly savings if cache hit-rate improves.
Priya: for model-selection semantics: we should let tenants pin a policy: "cost first" or "quality first". For "cost first" we allow lower min_coverage threshold to accept opportunistic routing. For "quality first" enforce strict coverage and prefer canonical model.
Josh: canary plan: enable opportunistic routing for 2 internal tenants at 5% traffic. Collect latency, success, and regression metrics. If no regressions, expand.
InfraBot: deploy scheduled: canary feature flag roll -> eng-platform-canary at 2026-03-25T18:30:00Z.
Sara: ok let's run the experiment. Priya will run rerank evaluation (A/B on held-out prompts) and post diffs. Dan will mock console widget and cost math. Josh will implement route proto and a toggle. Lee will add telemetry metrics (hit_coverage, effective_cost, cache_errors).
Priya: I'll run rerank_eval with following set: 10k queries sampled from production, measure nDCG and latency. Will post baseline vs canary by EOD tomorrow.
Dan: I'll sketch console mock in FigJam and drop link here when ready.
Lee: ops question — what if cache eviction causes flapping of routing choices? Need smoothing (e.g., 10-minute moving avg) before switching route.
Sara: good point; let's require moving avg coverage >= threshold for change. Also log routing decision with reason in trace.
Josh: added note: partial-hit accounting will need KV instrumentation to report token-level coverage. That's an infra change but straightforward.
Sara: thanks all. If no objections by EOD I'll open short RFC with experiments and console mocks. :white_check_mark:
